record.original_question: In low-energy antikaon-nucleon physics, is the isospin-0, orbital-angular-momentum-0 K−p quasi-bound state the traditional Λ(1405) resonance near 1405 MeV/c², or a higher-mass Λ*(1420)-like state associated with a two-pole structure, and what Σπ invariant-mass measurements can decisively determine its mass, width, and pole structure?

evidence.quote: This topic is related to a new puzzle in the physics of kaon-nucleon interaction: the nature of the Λ(1405) - single or double pole structure?

It is urgently important to distinguish the Λ∗ mass, 1405 or 1420 MeV/c2. A bubble-chamber Σπ invariant-mass data from stopped K− on 4He supports the Λ(1405) Ansatz [6]. A stopped K− on D experiment [7] would provide a decisive datum for the mass discrimination.
Where is the position of the I = 0 L = 0 K−p quasi-bound state? This question is directly connected to the strength of the s-wave I = 0 K¯N interaction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider low-energy antikaon–nucleon (K̄N) interactions in the strangeness S = −1, isospin I = 0, S-wave (orbital angular momentum L = 0) channel, where a quasi-bound state of the coupled K̄N–Σπ system manifests itself as the Λ(1405) hyperon resonance.

(a) Determine the precise location (real part of the pole) of the I = 0, L = 0 K⁻p quasi-bound state on the complex energy plane: is it the traditional Λ(1405), with mass ≈ 1405 MeV/c² and width ≈ 50 MeV, or is it a higher-mass state with mass ≈ 1420 MeV/c² (sometimes denoted Λ*(1420)) and a narrower width?

(b) Decide whether the observed resonance structure is described by a single pole of the coupled-channel scattering amplitude or by two poles situated between the πΣ and K̄N thresholds, and determine the masses, widths, and channel couplings of these poles.

(c) Specify which Σπ invariant-mass distribution measurements (e.g. from stopped K⁻ reactions on light nuclear targets such as ⁴He or deuterium) can decisively discriminate between the single-pole and two-pole hypotheses and pin down the pole positions and the strength of the s-wave I = 0 K̄N interaction.
artifact.status_search_result: The two-pole picture of the Λ(1405) is now strongly supported by chiral coupled-channel analyses, recent lattice QCD computations (2023–2024) of πΣ–K̄N scattering, and experiments by BGOOD, ALICE, and GlueX, and is reflected in the 2024 PDG review of the Λ(1405) pole structure. However, some analyses of CLAS and J-PARC data argue that a single resonance still suffices, so while the higher-mass narrow pole near 1420 MeV/c² is broadly accepted, the precise positions of both poles and the existence/nature of the lower pole remain under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Pole Structure of the Λ(1405) Region — PDG 2024 Review
status_evidence.snippet: PDG dedicated review on the two-pole structure of Λ(1405).
status_evidence.claim: The two-pole interpretation is established enough to warrant a dedicated PDG review.

status_evidence.title: Two-pole nature of the Λ(1405) from lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice QCD coupled-channel computation finds a virtual bound state below πΣ threshold plus a resonance pole below K̄N threshold.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice QCD supports the two-pole structure.

status_evidence.title: Identifying the two-pole structure of the Λ(1405) using an SU(3) flavor filter
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) analysis aims to discriminate the two poles via SU(3) flavor content.
status_evidence.claim: Active research in 2024 on resolving the two poles.

status_evidence.title: Pole trajectories of the Λ(1405) help establish its dynamical nature
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 study of pole trajectories consistent with lattice and experimental analyses.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing 2025 work on pole positions of Λ(1405).
